description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, known for its comforting warmth and rich, earthy flavor. This traditional recipe brings the authentic taste of Turkey to your kitchen with its simple yet robust ingredients and a hint of mint and chili from the sizzling butter topping. It's a nourishing and satisfying dish, perfect for any season.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lentils and Vegetables
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear; drain well. Chop the onion and carrot into small pieces, and mince the garlic. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and carrot and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Sprinkle in the all-purpose flour and cook for another minute, stirring, to create a roux-like base.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, then pour in the vegetable or chicken broth. Stir well to combine all ingredients. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup until it is smooth and creamy. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

instructions.title: Prepare the Butter Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foamy, remove it from the heat and stir in the dried mint and Aleppo pepper (pul biber). The spices will sizzle and release their aroma.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle a generous spoonful of the spiced butter topping over each serving. Serve immediately with a wedge of fresh lemon, which can be squeezed over the soup for extra brightness.

tips: For a truly authentic taste, do not skip the 'nane ve pul biberli tereyağı' (mint and chili butter) topping. It adds a crucial layer of flavor and aroma to the soup.
While red lentils are traditional, you can substitute with yellow lentils for a slightly different texture, though red lentils offer the best creamy consistency after blending.

Mercimek Corbasi tastes even better the next day. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a little water or broth if it has thickened too much.
article:
Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup, is more than just a dish; it's a warm embrace in a bowl, a staple that graces tables across Turkey from humble homes to elegant restaurants. This vibrant, creamy, and incredibly comforting soup holds a special place in Turkish cuisine, celebrated for its simplicity, nourishing qualities, and deeply satisfying flavor. Whether served as a hearty breakfast, a light lunch, or a comforting starter to a grand meal, Mercimek Corbasi embodies the soul of Turkish hospitality and culinary tradition.

Its appeal lies in its wholesome ingredients and the magic that happens when red lentils are simmered with aromatic vegetables and a touch of spice, then blended to a silky smooth perfection. Often finished with a drizzle of melted butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes, it’s a symphony of textures and tastes that is both humble and profoundly delicious. This article will guide you through the journey of understanding, preparing, and savoring this iconic Turkish Red Lentil Soup, ensuring you can recreate its authentic charm in your own kitchen. Get ready to dive into the world of one of Turkey’s most cherished dishes.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced "mer-jee-MEK chor-BAH-see," literally translates to "lentil soup." It is specifically a red lentil soup, distinguished by its characteristic creamy texture and often a beautiful reddish-orange hue. Originating from the rich culinary heritage of Anatolia, this soup has been a cornerstone of Turkish diets for centuries, valued for its affordability, nutritional density, and incredible flavor. Unlike some other lentil soups that might be chunky or rustic, Mercimek Corbasi is typically blended until smooth, giving it a velvety consistency that is incredibly soothing.

The base of the soup is simple: red lentils, onions, and often a touch of garlic and tomato paste for depth. What truly elevates it is the careful balance of seasonings, particularly dried mint (nane) and a hint of red pepper flakes (pul biber), which are frequently added as a finishing touch, sizzled in butter or olive oil. It’s a versatile dish, equally at home as a quick, energizing meal on a cold day or as an elegant starter before a more elaborate Turkish feast. Its widespread popularity is a testament to its comforting nature and universal appeal, making it one of the most recognized and adored Turkish soups and stews.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting an authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup requires a handful of simple, readily available ingredients. The quality of these components, though humble, significantly impacts the final taste.

*   **Red Lentils (Kırmızı Mercimek):** Approximately 1.5 cups. These cook quickly and break down easily, providing the soup's signature creamy texture. Always rinse them thoroughly before use.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped. Forms the aromatic base, adding sweetness and depth.
*   **Garlic:** 2-3 cloves, minced. Enhances the savory profile.
*   **Olive Oil:** 2 tablespoons. For sautéing the aromatics.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** 1 tablespoon. Adds a rich umami flavor and contributes to the soup's color.
*   **Water or Broth:** 6-7 cups (vegetable or chicken broth for richer flavor). The liquid medium for cooking the lentils.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste. Essential for seasoning.
*   **Dried Mint (Kuru Nane):** 1-2 teaspoons. A crucial herb that provides a distinctive, refreshing aroma.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber / Aleppo Pepper):** 1-2 teaspoons, or to taste. Adds a mild warmth and beautiful color to the final drizzle.
*   **Butter:** 2 tablespoons. For the traditional finishing drizzle (nane-pul biberli yağ) that adds richness and flavor.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** For serving. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice is indispensable for brightening the soup's flavors.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making this Turkish Red Lentil Soup is straightforward, even for novice cooks. Follow these steps to achieve a perfectly creamy and flavorful bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy. Drain well.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. Cooking the tomato paste helps to deepen its flavor and mellow its acidity.
4.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them with the onion and tomato mixture. Pour in the water or broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend the Soup:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (fill only halfway, vent the lid, and use a towel to hold it down) and blend until smooth. Return the blended soup to the pot.
6.  **Season:** Season the soup generously with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency.
7.  **Prepare the Chili-Mint Butter:** In a small saucepan or skillet, melt the butter over low heat. Once melted, add the dried mint and red pepper flakes. Sizzle for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Turkish Red Lentil Soup into bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the prepared chili-mint butter. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Turkish Red Lentil Soup involves a few key techniques and considerations:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial. Unrinsed lentils can make your soup starchy and cloudy. Rinsing also helps to prevent digestive discomfort for some people.
*   **Don't Skip the Tomato Paste Sauté:** Cooking the tomato paste for a minute or two before adding liquids caramelizes its sugars and deepens its umami flavor, adding a vital layer of complexity to the soup.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** The signature texture of Mercimek Corbasi is its velvety smoothness. An immersion blender makes this process incredibly easy. If using a regular blender, blend in batches and be cautious with hot liquids. Aim for no discernible lentil pieces.
*   **Adjust Consistency as Needed:** Red lentils absorb a lot of liquid. If your soup is too thick after blending, gradually stir in a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your preferred consistency. It should be creamy but still pourable.
*   **The Chili-Mint Butter is Non-Negotiable:** This finishing touch, known as "nane-pul biberli yağ," is what truly elevates this Turkish Red Lentil Soup. The warmth of the butter, the aromatic dried mint, and the gentle heat of the red pepper flakes transform the soup from good to extraordinary. Don't skip it!
*   **Taste and Adjust Seasoning:** Always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt and pepper. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end is also paramount; it brightens all the flavors and adds a tangy counterpoint that is essential to the authentic experience.

## Serving Suggestions

The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies not only in its taste but also in its versatility as a dish. While delicious on its own, a few traditional accompaniments elevate the experience of enjoying this Turkish Red Lentil Soup:

*   **Fresh Lemon Wedges:** This is arguably the most important accompaniment. A generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the soup's flavors, adding a zesty tang that cuts through the richness and enhances the overall taste profile. Always serve with lemon!
*   **Crusty Bread:** A staple with almost any Turkish meal, a good crusty bread (like a fresh Turkish simit or a simple baguette) is perfect for dipping into the creamy soup, soaking up every last drop of flavor.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or additional fresh mint leaves can add a burst of color and a fresh aroma to each bowl.
*   **Pickled Vegetables (Turşu):** In Turkey, it's common to serve soups with a side of pickled vegetables, such as pickled cucumbers, cabbage, or peppers. Their tangy, crunchy contrast is surprisingly delightful with the warm, smooth soup.
*   **Extra Red Pepper Flakes:** For those who enjoy a bit more heat, offer an extra sprinkle of pul biber at the table.
*   **Olives:** A small side dish of cured olives can also complement the soup beautifully.

Mercimek Corbasi can be enjoyed at any time of day. It's often served as a comforting breakfast, a light and satisfying lunch, or as the first course of a traditional Turkish dinner.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup is perfect as it is, its simple nature allows for some delightful variations and substitutions to suit different tastes or dietary needs.

*   **Make it Vegan:** The standard recipe is easily made vegan by ensuring you use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth and opting for olive oil in the final sizzle instead of butter, or using a plant-based butter alternative.
*   **Add Vegetables:** While the traditional version is smooth, you can add finely diced carrots or potatoes along with the lentils. They will cook down and blend seamlessly, adding extra nutrition and a subtle sweetness. Add them after sautéing the garlic and before adding the tomato paste.
*   **Spice it Up:** For a different flavor profile, consider adding a pinch of cumin or turmeric along with the tomato paste. Cumin adds an earthy warmth, while turmeric provides a lovely golden hue and mild, peppery notes.
*   **Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional, you can experiment with other dried herbs like oregano or thyme if you're looking for a slight deviation, though the essence of Mercimek Corbasi truly lies with the mint.
*   **Garnish Variations:** Besides the classic chili-mint butter, you could swirl in a spoonful of plain yogurt or a dollop of sour cream (for a non-vegan option) for extra creaminess and a tangy counterpoint. A drizzle of good quality extra virgin olive oil is also a simple and healthy alternative to butter.
*   **Different Lentils:** While red lentils are crucial for the classic creamy texture, you could make a similar soup with green or brown lentils, though it would have a different texture (often chunkier) and taste, evolving into a different kind of lentil soup altogether.

These variations allow you to customize this wonderful Turkish Red Lentil Soup to your liking, ensuring it remains a favorite in your culinary repertoire.

In conclusion, Mercimek Corbasi is a testament to the power of simple, wholesome ingredients transformed into something truly extraordinary. This Turkish Red Lentil Soup offers not just sustenance but a profound sense of comfort and a taste of the rich culinary traditions of Turkey. Its creamy texture, savory depth, and the vibrant finish of chili-mint butter, brightened by a squeeze of lemon, make it an unforgettable experience. Whether you're seeking a nutritious meal, a warming embrace on a chilly day, or an authentic foray into Turkish flavors, this humble yet magnificent soup is an absolute must-try. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the timeless charm of Mercimek Corbasi.
